newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes marginally firmer in two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes marginally firmer in two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed a shade up from New York's higher close on pre-market buying despite late selling near the end of a day of two-way trading, dealers said on Tuesday.
Bullion ended at US$339.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$339.10/60 close on Monday.

"Early buying boosted the gold prices due to overnight remarks from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto," a senior dealer at a local investment house said. "But a lack of follow-through buying interest after the local open and selling in late trade depressed the price."
"The market retained its bearish mantle and the price of gold will keep the range within US$337-341 in the short-term," another dealer added. "The metal will try the downside later."
Local gold ended HK$17 higher at HK$3,140 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -8.00.
